gao-gaoreports-gao-08-285t: In 2007 GAO briefed Congress on the hunt for nuclear terror plots: how ready were federal teams to spot and stop a smuggled bomb, and how safe were the posts that would lead the reply? The verdict was blunt — work remained. The report lists the weak spots in the nation's shield against the worst kind of attack.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-275t: Testimony from 2007 in which the Government Accountability Office turns the spotlight on itself: the diversity of its own Senior Executive Service. As the government's audit agency, GAO felt it should model the workforce diversity it often asks agencies to improve. The testimony reviews its recruitment, promotion, and mentoring efforts, and reports on how diverse its top leadership ranks had become.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-225t: A striking 2007 Government Accountability Office report: undercover tests exposed serious vulnerabilities in the Transportation Department's drug-testing program for safety-sensitive workers. Investigators found ways to cheat the tests used for truck drivers, pilots, and others whose jobs affect public safety. The report describes the exploits and demands fixes to a testing regime millions of workers depend on.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-255t: This 2007 Government Accountability Office testimony confronts long-standing concerns about how states finance their share of Medicaid. Some states used arrangements that shifted costs to the federal government in ways Congress never intended. GAO argues these schemes — documented over many years — support the need for stronger federal oversight of the joint state-federal health program's financing.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-135t: GAO told Congress in 2007 that the State Department's own watchdog was working with one hand tied. Short funds, thin access, and shaky standing kept the inspector general from fully grading U.S. diplomacy and aid. The briefing lays out the structural kinks — and argues that a watchdog that cannot bite is just a pet.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-215t: GAO gave Congress a split verdict on drug aid to Mexico in 2007: U.S. help had boosted the drug war south of the border, yet the northbound flow barely budged. The briefing captures the grind of a partnership winning skirmishes while losing the larger fight — and it fed a hard debate over whether the aid money was buying real results.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-95t: This 2007 Government Accountability Office testimony makes the case that 401(k) participants and plan sponsors need better information on fees. Hidden charges compound over a working lifetime, quietly shrinking retirement nest eggs. GAO argues that transparency — clear, comparable fee disclosures — is the fix. The testimony helped build the case for the fee-disclosure rules that would follow.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-115t: GAO warned Congress in 2007 that a new EPA rule could dim the public's view of toxic releases — the data that lets neighborhoods see what local plants puff out. Less public data hits poor and minority blocks hardest, GAO argued, since they already breathe the worst air. The briefing defends the right to know as an environmental justice issue.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1265t: Beds, services, and straight talk — GAO found all three wanting in the VA's homeless-vet housing aid in 2007. The grant program meant to shelter former troops was tripping over capacity gaps and poor outreach. The briefing maps where the help ran dry, and what it would take to get more vets under a roof.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1255t: Were federal agencies really buying small, and who was speaking up for the little guy? GAO's 2007 briefing shares notes from its sweep of agency small-business buying and the advocacy shops meant to defend it. The takeaway measures a promise Congress makes every year — keep federal dollars flowing to Main Street — against the receipts.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1245t: A handful of rail giants haul America's freight — and GAO's 2007 briefing hands Congress fresh numbers on what they charge. Rate trends and market-muscle questions fill the update. For farmers, factories, and shoppers downstream of the rails, the data fed the perennial debate: are the freight bills fair?
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1235t: Civilians shipped to war zones got murky medical promises in 2007, GAO told Congress — fuzzy rules on care and pay for hurt or sick deployed staff. The briefing lays out the policy fog around the Pentagon's civilian corps. Fairness, GAO argues, should not stop at the uniform's edge.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1135t: The export-control dam was springing leaks in 2007 — GAO's briefing says holes and red tape were defeating the system's guard over sensitive tech. The testimony warns that the gates meant to keep hot goods from cold rivals were failing. The findings demand a rebuild, not a patch.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1125t: The Pacific island pact was inching along in 2007 — GAO's briefing says compact work with the Marshall Islands progressed, but the big goals stayed distant. The testimony revisits the far-flung American promise. The findings ask the patient question: is the aid building a nation, or just a habit?
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1115t: The island-aid story got a retelling in 2007 — GAO's briefing again tracks the Marshall Islands compact's slow march. The testimony notes progress against the long horizon of self-rule. The findings keep the congressional eye on a promise made across an ocean.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1075t: The nation's guard plans were finally on paper in 2007 — GAO's briefing says the sector protection plans were done and the industry councils were finding their legs. The testimony marks a milestone in the long march to shield the lifelines. Plans complete, the briefing notes; the proving was next.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1095t: Energy bets were getting exotic in 2007 — GAO's briefing gives Congress an early read on derivatives trading and the regulator's grip on the market. The testimony previews the oversight questions that would soon turn urgent. The findings land just before the storm hit: the watchers were already worried.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1025t: Tearing down bleak towers to build mixed streets — GAO's 2007 briefing sizes up HOPE VI, the program remaking public housing. The testimony tracks the money, the watch, and the human results. The findings ask the hard question behind the bulldozers: did the new neighborhoods lift the old residents, or just move them?
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-995t: States were fumbling the trade-aid handoff in 2007 — GAO's briefing says the adjustment program needed changes so states could actually deliver the help. The testimony diagnoses the delivery gap in detail. The findings argue that benefits on paper are not benefits in hand.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-985t: VA bosses were getting bonuses in 2007 — GAO's briefing examines the payouts to senior executives at the veterans agency and what they rewarded. The testimony asks what the bonuses actually bought for veterans. The findings probe whether the rewards matched the results, or just the rank.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-935t: Sensitive data stayed at risk in 2007 despite the progress reports — GAO's briefing says agencies claimed gains while the crown jewels stayed exposed. The testimony punctures the happy talk with hard facts. The findings' refrain: reported progress is not the same as protection.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-895t: The government's attics and warehouses stayed a high-risk mess in 2007 — GAO's briefing updates Congress on the federal property sprawl. The testimony tracks the vacant, costly, and crumbling holdings. The findings' refrain: the nation's landlord still did not know what it owned.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-905t: American food aid was tripping over itself in 2007 — GAO's briefing says tangled rules sapped the efficiency of the hunger fight abroad. The testimony lists the snags slowing the grain. The findings ask an uncomfortable question: did the aid feed the hungry, or just the bureaucracy?
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-855t: Coal miners were still dying preventable deaths in 2007 — GAO's briefing says better watch by the mine agency and its federal partners could save them. The testimony demands sharper oversight underground. The findings' moral is old as mining: the seam does not forgive slack safety.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-835t: The next big storm was a when-not-if in 2007 — GAO's briefing sizes up DHS and FEMA's readiness for the catastrophic one. The testimony measures promises against machinery. The findings' unease is plain: the nation was better warned than prepared.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-795t: Selling America abroad was getting more professional in 2007 — GAO's briefing says public-diplomacy planning had improved, but execution still stumbled badly. The testimony balances credit with sharp critique. The findings argue that the message matters less than how it gets delivered.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-755t: April brought no relief for the Capitol's basement project in 2007 — GAO's briefing logs the Visitor Center's latest time overruns and costs. The testimony's refrain stayed grim quarter after quarter. The findings kept the congressional microscope fixed firmly on Congress's own money pit.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-785t: The food-safety system earned the high-risk label in 2007 — GAO's briefing says the designation could spotlight the government's fragmented watch. The testimony makes the case for the black mark. The findings argue that dinner should not be a gamble.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-525t: Iraq was a fraudster's paradise in 2007 — GAO's briefing says the conditions practically invited waste and abuse of the rebuild money. The testimony paints the free-for-all in stark terms. The findings warn that billions flowed exactly where the watchdogs could not follow.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-775t: Veterans' college aid was tangled in red tape in 2007 — GAO's briefing says overlapping approval chores needed real trimming. The testimony targets the duplication in detail. The findings argue that the benefit should not require a second education just to claim.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-685t: The new postal law was a toolbox in 2007 — GAO's briefing says the reform gave the mail service real ways to face its challenges. The testimony inventories the opportunities one by one. The findings' question lingers: would the tools get used, or just gather dust?
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-725t: The Smithsonian's roofs were leaking money in 2007 — GAO's briefing says funding the upkeep of the properties stayed a real challenge. The testimony tours the long list of deferred repairs. The findings' plea: the nation's attic should not crumble away from neglect.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-635t: The war on wasteful payments ground on in 2007 — GAO's briefing says the agencies kept working the improper-payment and recovery-audit rules. The testimony tracks the grind in detail. The findings' refrain: count the errors, chase the dollars, and repeat.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-595t: Life after the space shuttle was the question in 2007 — GAO's briefing examines the handoff to the next human spaceflight systems. The testimony probes the coming gap in detail. The findings warn that the ride to orbit had no guaranteed successor.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-625t: The FAA's money plumbing was being reworked in 2007, and GAO's briefing eyes the selected changes to the agency's funding structure. The testimony previews the stakes for travelers everywhere. The findings ask the blunt question: who would pay for the skies of tomorrow?
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-615t: The federal mortgage insurer was walking a tightrope in 2007, and GAO's briefing says its ability to manage risks would decide its financial fate. The testimony previews the danger. The findings warn that the housing backstop was only as strong as its risk controls.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-395t: Preparing for the next disaster was the 2007 theme, and GAO's briefing surveys Homeland Security's readiness and response posture. The testimony takes the full measure of the effort. The findings warn that the nation was better at planning the response than funding it.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-575t: The Coast Guard's big cutter program was troubled in 2007, and GAO's briefing reviews the Deepwater management fixes and the operational strains. The testimony takes stock. The findings warn that the fleet of the future needed steadier hands on the helm.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-545t: Transportation's troubles got a scorecard in 2007, and GAO's briefing lays out the challenges facing Congress and the department. The testimony inventories the gridlock in detail. The findings warn that the nation's arteries were clogging faster than the fixes. The roads were not waiting for Washington.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-385t: Iraq's rebuild got the auditor's full treatment in 2007, and GAO's briefing lays out the audit approach and the findings. The testimony shows the method and the mess. The findings warn that the billions needed both counting and accounting. The war's ledger was long.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-225t: Passenger rail security needed a leader in 2007, and GAO's briefing says enhanced federal leadership was required to guide the efforts. The testimony demands the command. The findings warn that the trains carried millions with too little guarding. The rails needed a real shield.
